headline: Executive order creates a National Health Information Technology Coordinator and promotes wider use of health information technology.
what_it_does: Based on its title, this order creates a new federal job called the National Health Information Technology Coordinator. It also calls for incentives to encourage the use of health information technology, such as electronic health records. No summary was provided, so the specific duties and incentives are not described here.

who_it_affects.group: Doctors, hospitals, and other health care providers
who_it_affects.how: They may be encouraged through federal incentives to adopt health information technology.
A new coordinator position is set up to lead federal work on health information technology.
Their health records may be more likely to be kept and shared electronically as providers adopt this technology.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed April 27, 2004; exact effective date not stated in the material provided.
